answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: No, do not add a 16-miler on Wednesday. Six days out, a long run cannot build fitness, it can only take sharpness and freshness away from Sunday. The heavy, flat feeling you have right now is exactly what a proper taper feels like, and it almost always lifts in the last three or four days. The best thing you can do this week is let the training settle: short runs, a little marathon pace to remind the legs what race effort feels like, and real rest on the rest days.

new.analysis:
You followed the week exactly as planned, which is the right thing to do heading into race week. Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday all landed within a few hundred metres of their targets, the quality session held 8:35/mi for 7 reps, and the 12-mile long run came in at 10:00/mi with a modest 7 bpm drift. Nothing in the numbers says you are losing fitness.

The heavy-leg, nervous feeling is the single most common taper experience and it is almost always a false alarm. Your easy pace has held at 9:51/mi and 139 bpm for a full month, your 20-miler three weeks ago drifted only 5 bpm over 3h 19m, and your marathon-pace work has sat right on sub-3:45 pace. That is a sharp runner, not a flat one.

The week ahead is built around one idea: arrive on the start line fresh. Volume drops by roughly a third from this week, the one bit of faster running on Wednesday is short and at goal pace only (around 8:34/mi), and Saturday is a true shakeout. On Sunday, run the first 10 miles controlled at 8:35 to 8:40, settle into 8:30 to 8:35 through 20, and only let it drop in the last 10k if you still feel in control. Eat and drink early and often, and resist the pull of anyone who goes out hot in the first mile.
